raw.text: The respondent was the owner of the entire premises and was occupying the ground floor at the time of the application.
The landlord required the premises bona fide for his occupation as a residence himself and his family members.
The tenant contended that the landlord's requirement for his occupation was not bona fide.
The Rent Controller accepted the tenant's plea that the requirement of the landlord for his occupation was not bona fide.
The High Court accepted the joint representation that the Tribunal had not recorded a finding on reasonably suitable residential accommodation and remanded the case.
The Tribunal held that the portion of premises in the landlord's occupation was not reasonably sufficient for a family consisting of the landlord, his wife, his son, son's wife and their children.
The Tribunal recorded a finding that the premises in the occupation of the respondent were not reasonably suitable for his residence.
